 [Newsworks = Reporter Heo Un-yeon] Typhoon Chanthu, the 30th of the season, is changing course eastward off the coast of Taiwan, heading toward Okinawa, Japan. It is not expected to make landfall on the Korean Peninsula, but South Korea will also be affected, including by rainfall.
 According to Kyodo News, the Japan Meteorological Agency warned on the 23rd that a large and very strong typhoon is moving northwest over the waters off the southern islands of Japan, and heavy rainfall could occur in the area.
 As of 5 a.m. that day, Chanthu was moving northwest over the sea south of Okinawa at 15 km/h, with a central pressure of 950 hPa.
 It is expected to pass near the islands southwest of Okinawa's main island by Saturday (the 24th) and weaken near the Tsushima Strait between Kyushu and the Korean Peninsula.
 The Japan Meteorological Agency forecasted that Okinawa Prefecture would receive up to 250 mm of rain over a 24-hour period by 6 a.m. on the 24th, with an additional 120 mm expected over the following 24 hours. If a frontal precipitation zone forms, the amount of precipitation may increase beyond this.
 According to Liberty Times, it will rain throughout Taiwan that day. Champi is expected to move away by the afternoon of the 24th, but heavy rain is likely to continue in northern and central Taiwan. On this day, major regions have taken proactive measures to prevent damage, including issuing leave-of-absence and school-closure orders. The stock market will also be closed for a day.
 Meanwhile, in Korea, rain will begin in the southern regions and Jeju Island starting the afternoon of the 23rd. The typhoon is pushing the moisture from the south toward our country, and rain will begin.
 According to the Korea Meteorological Administration, rain will begin in Jeju Island in the afternoon, spread to the Jeonnam and Gyeongnam regions at night, and then expand to the southern areas and Jeju Island on the 24th, while most of the rain in the Jeolla region will stop by the afternoon of the 25th, and in the inland Gyeongsang region and the southern coast by night.
 Precipitation from the 23rd to the 25th is expected to be 50–100 mm in Jeju (over 150 mm in mountainous areas), 20–60 mm in Busan, Ulsan, and Gyeongnam, 5–40 mm in Daegu and Gyeongbuk, and 20–60 mm in Gwangju and Jeonnam.
